`Pydantic v2 field_validator type mismatch field typed str validator returns list behavior`

💡 Result:

In **Pydantic v2**, what happens depends on the validator **mode**:

- **`mode='before'`**: whatever your validator returns is **validated against the field’s annotation** afterward. So if the field is typed `str` and your validator returns a `list`, you’ll get a validation error because the post-validator step still expects a `str`. [1]

- **`mode='after'` (default)**: your validator runs **after** Pydantic has already parsed/validated the input as a `str`. The validator’s return value becomes the field value; Pydantic is not doing another “validate against `str`” step after your function, so returning a `list` can “stick” and you end up with a runtime type mismatch on the model instance. [1]

- **`mode='plain'`**: Pydantic **skips internal validation against the field type entirely**, so returning a `list` for a `str` field is explicitly allowed (and will also “stick”). [1]

**Fix:** If the field is truly a `str`, ensure the validator always returns a `str` (or raise an error). If you actually want a `list`, change the field type to `list[...]` (or a `Union[...]`) so the model type matches what you return. [1]

**Source**  
[1] Pydantic docs: “Validators” (field validator modes and whether returned values are (re-)validated) https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/validators/
